examples.name: Sample (constructed) — make_scatter
paragraphs: Ten named points, one row each, x and y under the two printed axis titles. The plotted values are whole numbers by construction; on a printed page they would be estimates, judged with a tolerance.

examples.name: Sample — health-profile-europe-2024_p105

examples.name: Sample — db242_p2
paragraphs: Six bars printing their means, with footnote markers, and 95% confidence whiskers drawn but not printed. Each cell holds the printed centre, markers included, followed by the whisker ends read against the 0.50 grid. The dashed Adequate intake lines are reference ink: their labels follow the table as text. The whisker symbol before 95% confidence interval. is not text.

examples.name: Sample — climate-assessment-sdm_p7
paragraphs: Nothing is printed on any mark: centres and whisker ends are all estimates on the 0.5 grid. A three-panel figure, each panel its own table headed by its axis unit (°C): panel (a) has a single bar with no category label; in panel (b), Solar and volcanic drivers and Internal variability are drawn on the zero line, so their centre is 0, with whiskers either side. Panel (c) shows its first three bars, then the rest; its two bracket captions follow its table as text. The page heading and the figure caption below the panels are elided.

examples.name: Sample — ac8b3538-en_p131
paragraphs: Five bars with confidence whiskers, nothing printed: five rows, negatives included, each with its interval. The whisker ends are read at the drawn caps against the printed axis. The GHG-intensive occupations bar sits almost on zero: a relative tolerance means little there, so a checker widens it (0.3) rather than tightening the reading.

snippets.text:
Annex Figure 2.C.13. The incidence of job strain is lower in new and emerging and green-enhanced skills green occupations even when controlling for the job characteristics Marginal effect of the job strain indicator on the share of green-driven occupations, controlling for main individual and job characteristics, 2021 for Ostrevane Union members and 2015 for Borvika
%
Green-driven occupations -8.7 (-15–-2.6)
Green new and emerging occupations -11.5 (-17.2–-6.6)
Green-enhanced skills occupations -25 (-32.1–-19)
Green increased demand occupations 17 (7.2–26.6)
GHG-intensive occupations -1 (-9.3–7.3)
Note: The chart reports the point estimate (and 95% confidence intervals) of the percentage difference in the incidence of each type of green-driven occupation between job strained and not strained workers. Estimates come from a linear regression with the inverse hyperbolic sine of the share of each occupation type as dependent variable and a job strain dummy, occupation shares, education, gender, age, sector and country dummies as explanatory variables. The sample excludes Agriculture.

examples.name: Sample — charpy_verification_p24
paragraphs: Two box plots, both over the category HH-103, each its own table under its own figure caption, which tells them apart. Each box gives five readings against its axis; the printed annotation box and the labels of the dashed outlier-limit lines follow the table as text. The individual test values (crosses) and the mean marker carry no name and are not rows.
